subject: SIG follow-up: request for eviction traces and kv-cache isolation details
messages:
From: Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: bob.jenkins@fintech.io
Date: 2027-03-08T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: eviction traces and kv-cache isolation

Sergio — thanks again for the SIG doc last week. Security asked for a couple of concrete artifacts so we can close the item on dedicated tenancy: 

1) A short explanation of where the KV cache (session/prefix cache) lives for Dedicated: is it on-GPU memory, host DRAM, or a filesystem-backed store?
2) If eviction or preemption occurs under load (noisy neighbor), can you provide an anonymized eviction/scheduling trace for an example window (e.g., 5–10 minutes) showing when entries were evicted and the latency observed by the caller?
3) Any mitigations you have for noisy neighbor scenarios (cores pinned, GPU MIG, cgroup tuning, scheduler configs) — brief bullets are fine.

We can accept redacted logs; we mainly need timestamps, event types (evict/preempt/hot-restart), and rough token/latency impact. Attaching the partial SIG questionnaire (acme_SIG_partial.pdf) — items 3.2 / 3.5 reference these artifacts.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated delivery date?

Thanks,
Lara Nguyen
Security Engineer — Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_SIG_partial.pdf (pdf, 420KB)

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-08T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: eviction traces and kv-cache isolation

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: 

- KV cache residency: for Redwood Dedicated the KV cache we reference is an in-memory working set that lives in GPU device memory when the model runtime holds it, and falls back to host DRAM for larger KV footprints. We keep persistence off by design — there is no customer-shared filesystem for KV.
- Eviction traces: we can provide an anonymized scheduling/eviction trace (timestamps + event types + latency deltas) for a sampled window. Those will be sanitized to remove any request payloads or PII.
- Noisy neighbor mitigations: Dedicated pools are tenant-bound; we also have per-instance CPU/GPU affinity, preemption policies, and a conservative scheduler that prefers vertical scaling (burst capacity) before rescinding cores. We can bullet these in a single page doc.

I'll loop in Priyom and Hannah from infra to generate a sample log and a short explainer doc. Expect a sanitized sample and a 1–page isolation summary by EOD tomorrow (2027-03-09). If you need a specific window, tell us the timeframe and we'll prioritize that.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: isolation-briefing.pdf (stub, 180KB)

> On 2027-03-08T08:14:00-07:00, Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> > Sergio — thanks again for the SIG doc last week...

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: eviction traces and kv-cache isolation

Lara / Sergio — assigning this on the infra side. Quick notes on what I'll produce: 

- A sanitized log extract (kv-eviction-sample.log) showing event lines with ISO timestamps, event type (KV_EVICT / PREEMPT / SCHED_SCALE), instance id (redacted), and delta in observed p50/p95 latency. No request bodies, no client IDs.
- A 2-page explainer (kvcache-eviction-explainer.txt) describing the eviction policy (LRU-ish with token-cost weighting), how GPU memory vs host DRAM is used, and an example timeline that maps events to perceived latency.
- A brief statement on core residency: Dedicated pools are not time-sliced between customers at the PCIe/GPU level for pinned instances — we do not colocate distinct tenants on the same GPU hash/instance in Dedicated mode. There are some shared host processes (management/control plane) — we will list those exactly.

Request: please confirm the log window you prefer — we can pull a recent 10-minute window from 2027-03-04 14:00–14:10 PDT or generate one from a synthetic load run tomorrow. Also confirm if you want the logs delivered via secure Drive link or uploaded to your secure SFTP.

– Priyom
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-eviction-sample.log (stub, 28KB), kvcache-eviction-explainer.txt (stub, 6KB)

> On 2027-03-08T09:05:00-07:00, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai wrote:
> > Hi Lara — thanks for the clear ask...

From: Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: bob.jenkins@fintech.io
Date: 2027-03-09T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: eviction traces and kv-cache isolation

Thanks — the 2027-03-04 14:00–14:10 PDT window would work well for us; that's when we saw spikes in our in-house testing.

A couple of clarifying items for the sanitized log: 
- Please keep event timestamps and event types. Redact instance IDs but replace them with stable pseudonyms (e.g., instance-A, instance-B) so we can follow event flow.
- For latency deltas please include p50/p95 before and after an eviction event.
- Include an explicit line that states whether any GPU MIG partitions were used for those instances.

Delivery: secure Drive link is preferred. Also, if you can add a one-line confirmation about whether side-channel mitigations (retpoline/SMT off) are part of the Dedicated baseline, that would help our threat model.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Lara

> On 2027-03-09T10:22:00-07:00, priyom.das@redwood.ai wrote:
> > Lara / Sergio — assigning this on the infra side...

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: eviction traces and kv-cache isolation — next steps

Lara — thanks, team is on it. Short delivery plan: 

1) We will upload a sanitized 10-minute trace for 2027-03-04 14:00–14:10 PDT to the Drive folder linked below by EOD 2027-03-10. The trace will use pseudonyms for instance ids and include event timestamps, event types (KV_EVICT / PREEMPT / SCHED_SCALE), and p50/p95 latency snapshots pre/post event. File: kv-eviction-sample.log
2) Accompanying explainer (kvcache-eviction-explainer.txt) with algorithm summary, memory residency behavior (GPU vs host fallback), and a note: "Dedicated pools do not colocate distinct customer workloads on the same GPU partition; host-level control plane processes are shared but do not access runtime model memory."
3) Short answers: GPU MIG was not used in the sampled window; SMT was not globally disabled as part of the baseline — we will include a defender note listing recommended configurations for customers that require SMT disablement.

Deliverables: sanitized log + explainer + 1-page isolation summary in Drive. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cExampleLink

If Acme needs a signed attestation or additional artifacts (audit extracts, SOC 2 control mappings), let me know and we can coordinate with our compliance team.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none (links provided)
